_meta.indication: AYVAKIT is indicated for the treatment of adults with unresectable or metastatic GIST harboring a PDGFRA exon 18 mutation, including PDGFRA D842V mutations.

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, single-arm, dose-escalation, dose-expansion study; patients received avapritinib 300 mg or 400 mg orally once daily until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with unresectable or metastatic GIST harboring a PDGFRalpha exon 18 mutation (including PDGFRalpha D842V), regardless of prior therapy.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR), defined as confirmed CR or PR per mRECIST version 1.1 by central independent review.
pivotal_trials.n: Efficacy assessed in 43 patients with PDGFRalpha exon 18 mutations, including 38 with PDGFRalpha D842V mutations.
pivotal_trials.result: In the 43-patient PDGFRalpha exon 18 population, ORR was 84% (95% CI: 69, 93), including 3 complete and 33 partial responses; median DOR not reached. In the PDGFRalpha D842V subgroup, ORR was 89% (95% CI: 75, 97).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=20%) were edema, nausea, fatigue/asthenia, cognitive impairment, vomiting, decreased appetite, diarrhea, hair color changes, increased lacrimation, abdominal pain, constipation, rash, and dizziness. Serious risks include CNS effects (58% of 335 patients) and intracranial hemorrhage.
target_moa: Avapritinib is a tyrosine kinase inhibitor that targets PDGFRalpha and PDGFRalpha D842 mutants (and other exon 18 mutants) as well as multiple KIT exon 11, 11/17, and 17 mutants; these mutations can drive autophosphorylation and constitutive receptor activation supporting tumor cell proliferation.
companion_dx_detail: No companion diagnostic was approved at the time of approval; FDA imposed a postmarketing commitment for the sponsor to develop and submit the report of a valid companion diagnostic to detect PDGFRalpha D842V somatic variants.

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not presented to the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee or any other external consultants.

summary.text: NDA 212608 received regular (full) approval under 505(b)(1) for GIST with a PDGFRA exon 18 mutation. The application had priority review (granted August 1, 2019), orphan drug designation (January 6, 2016) and Fast Track designation (October 4, 2016), and was approved based on a single open-label, single-arm study (NAVIGATOR).
